chapter.title: Python Overview
chapter.summary: An introduction to Python: what it is, who created it, its key features, how to download and install it, the two modes of working in it, and how to write and run the classic "Hello World" program from the command line.

content.hinglish: Python ek high-level, general-purpose programming language hai jise Guido van Rossum ne banaya aur 1991 mein pehli baar release kiya gaya. Iski sabse badi khaas baat ye hai ki iska code padhne aur likhne mein bahut aasaan hai — bilkul simple English jaisa lagta hai. Python ek interpreted language hai, matlab code line-by-line chalta hai, alag se compile karne ki zaroorat nahi padti. Yahi wajah hai ki beginners aur badi companies dono ise pasand karte hain — web development se lekar data science aur AI tak har jagah Python ka use hota hai.
content.formalDefinition: Python is a high-level, interpreted, general-purpose, object-oriented programming language created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. It emphasises code readability through a clean, simple syntax, supports multiple programming paradigms (procedural, object-oriented and functional), and is platform-independent — the same source code runs on Windows, Linux and macOS without modification.
examples: Python is used to build websites and web apps with frameworks such as Django and Flask.
Data analysts use Python libraries like NumPy and pandas to process data.
Python powers machine-learning frameworks such as TensorFlow and scikit-learn.
Small automation scripts for file handling, reporting and web scraping are commonly written in Python.

tables.title: Key features of Python
rows: Easy to learn and read
Simple English-like syntax with fewer symbols than C/C++.
Interpreted
Code runs line by line through an interpreter; no separate compile step.
Free and open source
Anyone can download, use and modify it at no cost.
Platform independent
The same program runs on Windows, Linux and macOS (portable).
Object-oriented
Supports classes and objects along with procedural programming.
Large standard library
Comes with ready-made modules ('batteries included').
Extensible and embeddable
Can be extended with C/C++ and embedded in other applications.
Dynamically typed
Variable types are decided at run time; no type declaration needed.

diagrams:
SOURCE CODE (.py)
     |
     v
  INTERPRETER (reads one line at a time)
     |
     v
     OUTPUT on screen

(No separate machine-code file is produced.)

differences.title: Compiled vs Interpreted language
rows: Whole program is translated into machine code before running.
Code is translated and executed line by line at run time.
A separate executable file is produced.
No separate executable file is produced.
Errors are reported only after the whole program is compiled.
Errors are reported as soon as the faulty line is reached.
Generally faster execution.
Generally slower execution but faster to develop.
Compilation is a separate step from execution.
Translation and execution happen together.

content.pythonSyntax:
# This is a single-line comment in Python
print("Hello, World!")   # print() displays output on the screen

codeExamples.explanation: print() sends the text inside the quotes to the screen. The quotes mark the text as a string.
x and y store integers 5 and 7. print(x + y) adds them and displays the result 12.

commonMistakes: Thinking Python must be compiled first — Python is an interpreted language and runs directly.
Copying curly braces { } from C/Java; Python defines blocks using indentation instead.
Confusing the Python language with IDLE, which is only the editor and interactive shell that ships with Python.
Believing Python is 'only for beginners' — it is used in production by large organisations.
examNotes: Remember the exact spelling and the year: Guido van Rossum, first released in 1991.
For 'features of Python' questions, write at least four: interpreted, high-level, free and open source, portable, object-oriented, large library.
Python is a case-sensitive language: Print and print are treated as different names.
Python 3 is the current series; Python 2 reached end of life and is not used for new programs.
One-line definitions earn full marks in 1-mark questions — practise short, precise wording.

faqs.a: Python was developed by Guido van Rossum. Its development began in the late 1980s and it was first released in 1991.

faqs.q: Is Python a compiled or an interpreted language?
faqs.a: Python is an interpreted language — the interpreter reads and executes the code line by line, so no separate compilation step is needed by the programmer.

faqs.q: Why is Python called a high-level language?
faqs.a: Because its instructions resemble human language and hide the low-level details of the machine (memory, registers). The programmer writes in English-like syntax rather than machine or assembly code.
Yes. Python is free and open source — it can be downloaded from python.org, used, and modified without paying any licence fee.

quiz.question: Who is the creator of Python?
quiz.explanation: Python was created by Guido van Rossum; James Gosling created Java, Dennis Ritchie created C, and Bjarne Stroustrup created C++.

quiz.question: Python is a/an ______ language.
quiz.explanation: Python is an interpreted language: the interpreter executes the source code line by line.

quiz.question: Python was first released in the year ______.
quiz.explanation: Python was first released in 1991. (Development started around 1989, and Python 3 arrived in 2008.)

quiz.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Python?
quiz.explanation: Python is platform independent (portable), not platform dependent — the same code runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.

checklist: I can name the creator of Python and the year it was first released.
I can define Python as a high-level, interpreted, general-purpose language.
I can list at least four features of Python.
I can explain the difference between a compiled and an interpreted language.
I can give two real-world areas where Python is used.
I know that Python is case-sensitive and free/open source.

content.hinglish: Python ko install karna bahut aasaan hai — pehle official website python.org par jaake apne operating system (Windows/Mac/Linux) ke hisaab se latest installer download karte hain. Windows par .exe installer chalta hai jisme 'Add Python to PATH' ka checkbox hota hai — ise zaroor tick karna chahiye. Install hone ke baad IDLE bhi automatically mil jata hai, jo Python ka default editor aur interactive shell hai. Command line par python --version ya python3 --version type karke confirm kar sakte hain ki Python theek se install hua hai.
content.formalDefinition: Installing Python means obtaining the official Python interpreter from python.org and setting it up on the computer so that Python programs can be written and executed. The standard Windows installer also installs IDLE (Integrated Development and Learning Environment). During installation, the option 'Add Python to PATH' registers the Python interpreter with the operating system so that the command 'python' works from any directory in the terminal.
examples: Download the Windows installer from the Downloads page of python.org and run python-3.x.x.exe.
Tick 'Add Python to PATH' in the installer so that the 'python' command works from any folder.
After installation, open IDLE from the Start menu to write and run Python programs.
Verify the installation by typing 'python --version' in the command prompt.

tables.title: Installation steps on Windows
rows: Open a browser and go to the official website www.python.org.
Go to Downloads and choose the Windows installer for the latest version.
Run the downloaded .exe file.
Tick the checkbox 'Add Python to PATH' at the bottom of the installer window.
Click 'Install Now' and wait for the setup to finish.
Click Close; IDLE and the Python interpreter are now installed.
Open Command Prompt and type 'python --version' to confirm the installation.

diagrams:
www.python.org  ->  Downloads  ->  Windows installer (.exe)
        |
        v
  Run installer
        |
  [x] Add Python to PATH
        |
        v
  Install Now  ->  IDLE + python.exe installed
        |
        v
  Command Prompt: python --version  ->  Python 3.x.x

differences.title: PATH not set vs PATH set
rows: The command 'python' is not recognised in the terminal.
The command 'python' works from any folder.
You must type the full path, e.g. C:\Python311\python.exe.
You can simply type python or python3.
Running scripts from other folders is inconvenient.
Scripts can be run from anywhere in the terminal.

content.pythonSyntax:
# Check the installed Python version (run these in the terminal, not inside Python):
python --version
python3 --version

# Start the Python interactive shell:
python

codeExamples.explanation: Typed in the command prompt/terminal, this command prints the installed Python version and confirms that Python is available on the PATH.
This runs the script file hello.py using the Python interpreter from the terminal.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to tick 'Add Python to PATH', after which the 'python' command is not recognised in the terminal.
Downloading Python from unofficial websites instead of the official python.org.
Installing a very old version (such as Python 2) instead of the current Python 3 series.
Typing Python code directly into the command prompt instead of the Python interactive shell or IDLE.
examNotes: The official website for downloading Python is www.python.org — remember this exact address.
IDLE is bundled with the standard Python installation; no separate download is needed.
The 'Add Python to PATH' option registers Python with the operating system so the 'python' command works everywhere.
To confirm the installation, run 'python --version' (or 'python3 --version') in the terminal.
pip, the package installer for Python, is also installed along with Python 3.

faqs.q: From where should Python be downloaded?
faqs.a: Only from the official website, www.python.org, to ensure a safe and genuine installation.

faqs.q: What does 'Add Python to PATH' do?
faqs.a: It registers the Python interpreter with the operating system's PATH environment variable, so you can run the 'python' command from any folder in the terminal without typing the full path.
No. IDLE comes bundled with the standard Python installation and is available from the Start menu after installation.

faqs.q: How do I check whether Python is installed correctly?
faqs.a: Open the command prompt or terminal and type 'python --version'. If it prints a version such as Python 3.11.4, the installation was successful.

quiz.question: The official website for downloading Python is ______.
quiz.explanation: Python is downloaded from its official site www.python.org.

quiz.question: Which option should be ticked during Windows installation so the 'python' command works from any folder?
quiz.explanation: 'Add Python to PATH' registers the interpreter with the operating system so the python command works from anywhere.

quiz.question: Which editor/shell is bundled with the standard Python installation?
quiz.explanation: IDLE (Integrated Development and Learning Environment) ships with Python; the others are separate tools.

quiz.question: Which command confirms the installed Python version in the terminal?
quiz.explanation: 'python --version' prints the installed version and confirms Python is on the PATH.

checklist: I know the official website python.org for downloading Python.
I can list the steps to install Python on Windows.
I can explain what 'Add Python to PATH' does.
I know that IDLE is bundled with the Python installation.
I can verify an installation using 'python --version'.
I know Python 3 is the current series to install.

content.hinglish: Python mein kaam karne ke do main tareeke hote hain — interactive mode aur script mode. Interactive mode mein aap >>> prompt par ek-ek line likhte hain aur Enter dabate hi turant result dikh jata hai; yeh chhote experiments aur testing ke liye achha hai. Script mode mein poora program ek file mein likha jata hai jise .py extension ke saath save karte hain, aur phir use poora ek saath run karte hain. IDLE dono kaam karta hai — isme shell (interactive) aur File > New File se editor (script) milta hai. Bade programs ke liye script mode hi behtar hota hai kyunki code save rehta hai aur dobara use ho sakta hai.
content.formalDefinition: Working in Python refers to the two ways of executing Python code: interactive mode, in which each statement is typed at the '>>>' prompt and executed immediately, and script mode, in which the complete program is written in a file with the .py extension and executed as a whole. IDLE (Integrated Development and Learning Environment) provides both an interactive shell and a file editor, allowing programmers to test statements quickly and to save and run complete programs.
examples: Interactive: type 2 + 3 at the >>> prompt and press Enter; 5 appears immediately.
Script: write print('Hello') in a new file, save it as hello.py and run it with F5 in IDLE.
Interactive is used to test a single statement; script mode is used to build a complete program.
In IDLE, File > New File opens the editor, and Run > Run Module (F5) executes the saved script.

tables.title: Interactive mode vs Script mode
rows: How it is used
Type one statement at a time at the >>> prompt.
Write the whole program in a file.
Result shown
Immediately after pressing Enter.
Only when the whole script is run.
Saving
Code is not saved permanently.
Code is saved in a .py file and can be reused.
Suitable for
Testing small expressions and quick checks.
Writing complete, longer programs.
print() needed?
Not always — the value is echoed automatically.
Yes — you must use print() to see output.
Editing
Difficult to correct earlier lines.
Easy — the file can be edited and re-run.

diagrams:
WORKING IN PYTHON
  |
  +-- Interactive mode (>>>)  --->  type line -> Enter -> result now
  |
  +-- Script mode (.py file)  --->  write file -> save -> Run (F5) -> output

IDLE = Integrated Development and Learning Environment
  [>>> shell]  +  [File > New File editor]

differences.title: IDLE shell vs IDLE editor
rows: Shows the >>> prompt.
A blank window to type a program file.
Executes each statement as soon as Enter is pressed.
Executes the whole program only when run (F5).
Good for quick testing.
Good for writing and saving full programs.
Cannot save the session as a program file.
Saved with a .py extension.

content.pythonSyntax:
# --- Interactive mode (typed at the >>> prompt) ---
>>> 2 + 3
5
>>> print("Hi")
Hi

# --- Script mode (a .py file, run as a whole) ---
a = 4
b = 6
print("Sum =", a + b)

codeExamples.explanation: In interactive mode the value of the expression is displayed automatically at the >>> prompt — no print() is needed.
In script mode you must use print() to display the result; simply writing a + b would produce no visible output.

commonMistakes: Expecting an expression like a + b to print itself in script mode — print() is required.
Saving a script without the .py extension, so it is not recognised as a Python file.
Pasting multi-line code into the interactive shell and expecting it all to run at once.
Forgetting to save the file before pressing F5 in IDLE, so the old version runs.
examNotes: The interactive prompt is >>> and the prompt for a continuation line is ... .
In interactive mode the result of an expression is shown automatically; in script mode you must use print().
A Python script file must be saved with the .py extension.
In IDLE, File > New File opens the editor and Run > Run Module (or F5) runs the script.
IDLE stands for Integrated Development and Learning Environment.
Script mode is preferred for complete programs because the code is saved and can be reused and edited.

faqs.q: What are the two modes of working in Python?
faqs.a: Interactive mode (statements typed at the >>> prompt and executed immediately) and script mode (a complete program saved in a .py file and run as a whole).

faqs.q: Which mode is better for writing a long program?
faqs.a: Script mode, because the entire program is saved in a file, can be edited easily and can be re-run many times.
IDLE (Integrated Development and Learning Environment) is the simple editor and interactive shell that comes bundled with Python. It provides both a >>> shell and a file editor.

faqs.q: How do I run a script in IDLE?
faqs.a: Open or create the file, save it with a .py extension, then choose Run > Run Module or press F5.

quiz.question: Which prompt is shown in Python's interactive mode?
quiz.explanation: Python's interactive mode uses the >>> prompt; the $ prompt is a shell prompt and # begins a comment.

quiz.question: In which mode must you use print() to see the output of an expression?
quiz.explanation: In interactive mode the value is echoed automatically, but in script mode you must use print() to display a result.

quiz.question: A Python program file is saved with the extension ______.
quiz.explanation: Python script files use the .py extension.

quiz.question: Which key runs a script from the IDLE editor?
quiz.explanation: F5 (Run > Run Module) executes the current script in IDLE. Ctrl+S is used to save.

checklist: I can name the two modes of working in Python.
I can explain how interactive mode differs from script mode.
I know the interactive prompt is >>>.
I know Python files use the .py extension.
I can create, save and run a file in IDLE using File > New File and F5.
I know IDLE stands for Integrated Development and Learning Environment.

topics.title: Printing "Hello World" using the Command Line

content.hinglish: Kisi bhi nayi language mein pehla program aksar 'Hello World' print karna hota hai. Python mein iske liye print() function use karte hain — print("Hello World"). Command line se ise do tareeke se chala sakte hain: pehle 'python' likhkar interactive shell (REPL) kholo aur seedha statement type karo, ya ek file hello.py banao aur terminal par 'python hello.py' likh kar chalao. REPL ka matlab hai Read-Eval-Print Loop — jo aap type karte hain use padhta hai, chalata hai aur result dikhata hai, phir dobara prompt deta hai.
content.formalDefinition: Printing 'Hello World' is the traditional first program in a new language. In Python it is written using the built-in print() function: print("Hello World"). It can be run from the command line either by entering the Python interactive shell (REPL — Read, Eval, Print, Loop) and typing the statement at the >>> prompt, or by saving the statement in a file such as hello.py and executing it with the command 'python hello.py'.
examples: print("Hello World") — the classic first program.
At the terminal: python hello.py runs the saved program.
At the >>> prompt: typing print("Hello World") and pressing Enter shows Hello World at once.
print("Hello", "World") prints Hello World with a space between the two values.

tables.title: Running 'Hello World' two ways
rows: Interactive shell (REPL)
python  then  print("Hello World")
Hello World is printed immediately at the >>> prompt.
Script file
Save print("Hello World") in hello.py, then run python hello.py
The interpreter runs the file and prints Hello World.
IDLE editor
Type the statement and press F5
The saved script runs and prints Hello World.

diagrams:
REPL = Read -> Eval -> Print -> Loop

C:\> python
>>> print("Hello World")
Hello World
>>>

OR

C:\> python hello.py
Hello World

differences.title: print("Hello" + "World") vs print("Hello", "World")
rows: print("Hello" + "World") gives HelloWorld
print("Hello", "World") gives Hello World
Values are joined with no space.
Values are separated by a space by default.
Only strings can be joined with +.
Values of any type can be separated by commas.

content.pythonSyntax:
print(value1, value2, ..., sep=' ', end='\n')

# Examples
print("Hello World")
print("Hello", "World")
print("Hello", "World", sep="-")
print("Hello", end=" ")
print("World")

codeExamples.explanation: The text inside quotes is a string; print() displays it followed by a newline.
The sep parameter replaces the default space separator with a hyphen.
end=" " makes the first print() end with a space instead of a newline, so the second print() continues on the same line.

commonMistakes: Forgetting the quotes: print(Hello World) is treated as two undefined names and causes a NameError.
Using a capital P — Print is not the same as print in case-sensitive Python.
Running python hello.py from the wrong folder, causing a 'file not found' error.
Expecting a space when using + : print("Hello" + "World") gives HelloWorld, not Hello World.
examNotes: print() is a built-in function; its arguments may be strings, numbers or variables.
The default separator (sep) is a space and the default line terminator (end) is a newline (\n).
REPL stands for Read, Eval, Print, Loop — the behaviour of the interactive shell.
The command to run a saved script from the terminal is: python filename.py
To print Hello World on one line from the terminal, either use the shell directly or run a .py file.

faqs.a: REPL stands for Read, Eval, Print, Loop. It describes the Python interactive shell: it reads what you type, evaluates it, prints the result, and then loops back to the prompt.

faqs.q: How do I run hello.py from the command line?
faqs.a: Open the terminal in the folder containing the file and type: python hello.py (use python3 hello.py on some systems). The output is printed below.

faqs.q: What is the difference between print("Hello"+"World") and print("Hello","World")?
faqs.a: The + joins the strings with no space giving HelloWorld, while the comma separates the values with a space giving Hello World.

faqs.q: Why do we need quotes in print("Hello World")?
faqs.a: Quotes mark the text as a string literal. Without quotes, Python would try to interpret Hello and World as variable names and raise a NameError.

quiz.question: Which function is used to display output in Python?
quiz.explanation: print() is Python's built-in function for displaying output on the screen.

quiz.question: What is the output of print("Hello", "World")?
quiz.explanation: A comma between arguments makes print() separate them with a single space by default.

quiz.question: What does REPL stand for?
quiz.explanation: REPL = Read, Eval, Print, Loop — the cycle followed by the interactive Python shell.

quiz.question: Which command runs a saved script named hello.py from the terminal?
quiz.explanation: The interpreter is invoked as 'python' followed by the script filename: python hello.py.

checklist: I can write the Hello World program in Python.
I know that print() is used to display output.
I can run Hello World both interactively and from a script file.
I know the terminal command 'python hello.py'.
I can explain what REPL stands for.
I know the default values of the sep and end parameters.

questions.question: Who is the creator of Python?
optionExplanations: Java was created by James Gosling.
Correct — Python was created by Guido van Rossum.
C was created by Dennis Ritchie.
C++ was created by Bjarne Stroustrup.
questions.explanation: Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991.

questions.question: Python is a/an ______ language.
optionExplanations: A compiled language needs a separate translation step.
Correct — Python is interpreted.
Assembly is a low-level language.
Machine-level code is binary and not written by hand.
questions.explanation: Python is an interpreted language: the interpreter executes the source code line by line.

questions.question: In which year was Python first released?
optionExplanations: 1989 is when development started.
Correct — Python was first released in 1991.
2000 is when Python 2.0 was released.
2008 is when Python 3.0 was released.
questions.explanation: Development began in the late 1980s but Python was first released in 1991.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Python?
optionExplanations: Correct — Python is platform INDEPENDENT (portable), not platform dependent.
Python is free and open source.
Python is a high-level language.
Python is an interpreted language.
questions.explanation: Python is platform independent — the same code runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.

questions.question: Which extension is used for a Python program file?
optionExplanations: .python is not a Python extension.
Correct — Python files use .py.
.pyt is not standard.
.pt is used by other tools (e.g. PyTorch models).
questions.explanation: Python script files are saved with the .py extension.

questions.question: Which mode executes each statement immediately and shows the result at once?
optionExplanations: Script mode runs the whole file together.
Correct — interactive mode executes statements one at a time.
Batch mode is not a Python working mode.
Compile mode is not a Python working mode.
questions.explanation: In interactive mode a statement is executed as soon as Enter is pressed.

questions.question: What is the prompt shown in Python's interactive mode?
optionExplanations: $ is an operating-system shell prompt.
Correct — Python uses >>>.
# begins a comment in Python.
>> is not the Python prompt.
questions.explanation: The Python interactive shell displays the >>> prompt; a continuation line uses ...

questions.question: From which website should Python be downloaded?
optionExplanations: python.com is not the official site.
Correct — the official site is www.python.org.
python.net is not the official site.
pypi is a package index, not the download site.
questions.explanation: Python is downloaded from its official website, www.python.org.

questions.question: Which editor and interactive shell is bundled with the standard Python installation?
optionExplanations: PyCharm is a separate third-party IDE.
Correct — IDLE ships with Python.
VS Code is a separate editor.
Jupyter is installed separately.
questions.explanation: IDLE (Integrated Development and Learning Environment) is bundled with Python.

questions.question: How are blocks of code defined in Python?
optionExplanations: Curly braces are used in C, Java and JavaScript.
Correct — Python uses indentation.
Parentheses group expressions, not blocks.
begin/end are used in Pascal, not Python.
questions.explanation: Python uses indentation (whitespace) to define blocks such as those of if, for and while.

questions.question: Which function is used to display output in Python?
optionExplanations: echo is a shell command, not a Python function.
printf() is used in C.
Correct — print() displays output.
display() is not a standard Python output function.
questions.explanation: print() is Python's built-in function for displaying output on the screen.

questions.question: Python is a case-sensitive language. This means that ______.
options: Print and print are the same
Print and print are different names
keywords can be written in any case
optionExplanations: They are not the same.
Correct — Print and print are different identifiers.
Case is never ignored in Python.
Keywords must be written in the correct case.
questions.explanation: In a case-sensitive language, Print and print are treated as different names.

questions.question: Which function tells you the data type of a value?
optionExplanations: datatype() is not a Python function.
Correct — type() returns the data type.
typeof() is used in JavaScript.
class() is not used for this purpose.
questions.explanation: The built-in function type(x) returns the data type of x, e.g. <class 'int'>.

questions.question: What is printed by print("A", "B", sep="-")?
optionExplanations: That would be the default separator.
Correct — sep="-" uses a hyphen.
The comma is not printed.
There is a separator between the values.
questions.explanation: The sep parameter sets the string placed between multiple arguments; here it is a hyphen.

questions.question: The ability of the same Python program to run on different operating systems is called ______.
optionExplanations: Compilation is translation of code, not this property.
Correct — it is portability.
Conversion is unrelated.
Interpretation is how code is executed, not this property.
questions.explanation: Portability (platform independence) means the same source code runs on Windows, Linux and macOS.

questions.question: Which Python version series is the current one used for new programs?
optionExplanations: Python 1 is obsolete.
Python 2 reached end of life and is not used for new code.
Correct — Python 3 is the current series.
Python 4 does not exist yet.
questions.explanation: Python 3 is the current series; Python 2 is no longer supported.

questions.question: Which of the following is a correct single-line comment in Python?
optionExplanations: // is used in C, Java and JavaScript.
/* */ is a C-style block comment.
Correct — Python uses #.
-- is not a Python comment.
questions.explanation: In Python a comment begins with # and extends to the end of the line.

questions.question: What does the end parameter of print() control?
options: The character printed at the end of the output
optionExplanations: That is not what end does.
Correct — end sets what is printed after the values.
end does not set a line count.
That is the job of the sep parameter.
questions.explanation: The end parameter sets what is printed after the values; by default it is a newline (\n).

questions.question: In script mode, to display the value of an expression you must use ______.
optionExplanations: echo is a shell command.
Correct — print() is required in script mode.
write() writes to a file, not the screen.
show() is not a Python function.
questions.explanation: In script mode values are not echoed automatically; print() must be used to display them.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a built-in Python data type?
optionExplanations: int is a built-in integer type.
float is a built-in floating-point type.
str is a built-in string type.
Correct — Python has no separate char type; a single character is a str.
questions.explanation: Python has no char data type; characters are stored as strings of length one.

questions.question: Python is often described as a 'batteries included' language because ______.
options: it ships with a large standard library
it is only used for hardware
optionExplanations: Python does not need batteries.
Correct — it comes with a large standard library.
It is not limited to hardware.
That is unrelated to the phrase.
questions.explanation: 'Batteries included' means Python ships with a large standard library of ready-to-use modules.

questions.question: Which statement about Python is TRUE?
options: Python is a high-level, interpreted language
optionExplanations: Python is high-level, not low-level.
Python is interpreted.
Correct — Python is high-level and interpreted.
Python supports object-oriented programming.
questions.explanation: Python is a high-level, interpreted, general-purpose and object-oriented language.

questions.question: What is the output of print("2" + "3")?
optionExplanations: 5 would be the result of adding the numbers 2 and 3.
Correct — the + joins two strings to give 23.
Quotes are not part of the output.
There is no error; + joins two strings.

questions.question: Explain the role of the .py extension and how Python executes a script file.
questions.modelAnswer: The .py extension identifies a file as a Python source (script) file, so the operating system and editors recognise it as Python code. When such a file is executed — for example by the command python hello.py or by pressing F5 in IDLE — the Python interpreter reads the file, executes its statements from top to bottom, and displays any output produced by print(). The code is not converted into a separate machine-code file; the interpreter handles the whole process. Saving with .py is therefore essential for a program to be treated as a Python script.

questions.question: Compare compiled and interpreted languages, and explain why Python is called an interpreted language with two advantages and one disadvantage.
questions.modelAnswer: In a compiled language (such as C or C++), the entire source program is translated into machine code by a compiler before it is run, and a separate executable file is produced; errors are reported only after the whole program is compiled. In an interpreted language, the source code is translated and executed line by line by an interpreter at run time, and no separate executable file is produced; errors are reported as soon as the faulty line is reached. Python is called an interpreted language because the Python interpreter reads and executes its source code line by line (internally it first compiles to bytecode, but the programmer sees only interpretation, with no separate compile step). Advantages of being interpreted: (i) development is faster because there is no compile step and code can be run immediately; (ii) errors are pinpointed to the exact line, which makes debugging easier, and the code is portable. Disadvantage: interpreted programs generally execute more slowly than fully compiled programs because translation happens at run time.

questions.question: Explain the two modes of working in Python — interactive mode and script mode — with examples, and describe how to create and run a .py file in IDLE.
questions.modelAnswer: Python code can be executed in two modes. (1) Interactive mode: the interpreter is started and a >>> prompt appears; each statement is typed and, on pressing Enter, executed immediately with the result displayed at once. For example, typing 2 + 3 at the prompt shows 5 without any print(). This mode is ideal for testing small expressions but the code is not saved. (2) Script mode: the complete program is written in a file and saved with the .py extension; the whole file is then executed together. For example, saving a = 4; b = 6; print("Sum =", a + b) in sum.py and running it prints Sum = 10. In script mode print() must be used to display output, but the code is saved, editable and reusable. To create and run a script in IDLE: open IDLE, choose File > New File to open the editor, type the program, save it with a .py extension using File > Save, and run it with Run > Run Module or the F5 key. The output appears in the IDLE shell. IDLE therefore provides both the interactive shell and the file editor.

questions.question: Write a detailed note on the print() function, covering its syntax, the sep and end parameters, printing multiple values, and string concatenation versus the comma.
questions.modelAnswer: The print() function is Python's built-in function for displaying output on the screen. Its general form is print(value1, value2, ..., sep=' ', end='\n'). Values may be strings (in quotes), numbers or variables. When several values are given separated by commas, print() displays them separated by a space — for example print("Hello", "World") gives Hello World. The sep parameter changes this separator: print("A", "B", sep="-") gives A-B. The end parameter sets what is printed after the values; the default is a newline (\n), so each print() starts a new line. Using end=" " keeps the cursor on the same line, so print("Hello", end=" ") followed by print("World") gives Hello World on one line. Values can also be joined with the + operator, but + concatenates strings with no space — print("Hello" + "World") gives HelloWorld — and it works only for strings, whereas a comma can separate values of any type. The simplest program, print("Hello World"), prints Hello World and is the traditional first program in Python.

questions.question: Write the exact output produced by the following code.
questions.code:
x = 10
y = 3
print(x + y)
print(x // y)
print(x % y)
print(x ** y)
executionSteps: x is assigned 10 and y is assigned 3.
print(x + y) prints 13 (addition).
print(x // y) prints 3 (integer/floored division: 10 // 3 = 3).
print(x % y) prints 1 (remainder: 10 % 3 = 1).
print(x ** y) prints 1000 (power: 10 raised to 3).
questions.explanation: This tests arithmetic operators: +, // (floored division), % (modulus) and ** (exponent).

questions.question: The following program runs without error but produces a wrong result. Identify the type of error and write the corrected code.
questions.code:
length = 10
breadth = 5
area = length + breadth
print("Area =", area)
questions.correctAnswer:
length = 10
breadth = 5
area = length * breadth
print("Area =", area)
executionSteps: The program runs and prints Area = 15, but the area of a rectangle is length x breadth.
Using + instead of * gives the sum, not the area — this is a logical error.
Replacing + with * gives area = 10 * 5 = 50.
The corrected program prints Area = 50.
questions.explanation: A logical error produces a valid but incorrect result; here the wrong operator was used.

questions.question: The following program stops with an error when run. Identify the type of error and write a corrected version that does not crash.
executionSteps: The statement print(a / b) attempts to divide 10 by 0.
Division by zero is not allowed, so Python raises a ZeroDivisionError at run time.
This is a runtime error — the program starts but fails while running.
Checking b != 0 before dividing prevents the crash and prints a helpful message instead.
questions.explanation: A runtime error occurs during execution; guarding against division by zero avoids the ZeroDivisionError.
